caption: Samaltak · Live. Everything in this video changes a running system, driven through samaltak-ctl. Co-star: Claude's Robot.
spoken: [excited] Okay, this one's fun! Everything here changes a running system. No restarts, no tricks. Meet our co-star: Claude's Robot, modelled on Claude Shannon's juggling machine.

caption: The theme is a Smalltalk class: change the accent in the System Browser, ⌘S, and every window restyles at once.
spoken: Let's start with the look. The theme is just a class. Change the accent colour, save, and [pause] every window picks it up, while the robot keeps juggling.

caption: The GPU shader is Metal source, a string in a Smalltalk method (Renderer class>>shaderSource). ⌘S compiles it into a new GPU pipeline.
spoken: The GPU shader isn't Smalltalk, it's Metal source, kept as a string in a Smalltalk method. Edit it, save, and Smalltalk builds a new GPU pipeline. [pause] Scan lines! Okay, putting that back.

caption: The compositor, the Process that puts every window on screen each frame, is Smalltalk: deeper, ultramarine shadows, ⌘S.
spoken: [upbeat] The compositor, the process that puts every window on screen, is Smalltalk too. So let's change it while it runs. Big blue shadows, [pause] on every window at once!

caption: Glyphs are rasterized in Smalltalk from the .ttf on disk: flip the coverage, and every glyph turns inside out.
spoken: Fonts are rasterized in Smalltalk, straight from the TrueType file. Flip the coverage, and [pause] every glyph on screen turns inside out! These are the actual pixels. And back.

caption: One setting slows the animation clock tenfold: the menu, a window opening, the selection glide.
spoken: Now let's slow time down, ten times, so you can see every little animation.

caption: Edit and continue: change the robot's ball colour while it juggles. The next frame uses it.
spoken: Edit and continue? Change the colour of the balls, mid-act, save, and [pause] the very next frame uses it.

caption: An infinite loop in the robot's step: its window hangs, everything else stays smooth. ⌘. and Debug: the debugger shows the loop.
spoken: [upbeat] Now let's break things! An infinite loop, right in the robot's step. Save, and [pause] it hangs, but everything else stays smooth. Command-period, debug, and there's our loop.

caption: Delete the loop in the debugger: ⌘S recompiles and restarts the frame. Proceed, and it juggles again.
spoken: Delete it right there in the debugger, save, proceed, and [pause] it's juggling again!

caption: A breakpoint in move:, only for the robot's Process: the balls freeze mid-air, the rest of the system keeps running.
spoken: Next, a breakpoint in move, just for the robot's process. The balls freeze mid-air, [pause] and everything else still works.

caption: Flip gravity in the debugger (0 @ 0.4 becomes 0 @ -0.4), ⌘S, Proceed: the balls fall upward.
spoken: [mischievously] Now flip gravity, right in the debugger. Save, proceed, and [pause] the balls fall up!

caption: Gravity back in the System Browser; a click puts the balls back into the robot's hands.
spoken: Okay, gravity back, and a click hands the robot its balls again.

caption: Freeze the robot mid-throw, save the image with the debugger open, quit.
spoken: Now freeze it mid-throw, save the image, debugger and all, and quit.

caption: Relaunch: the robot is back, frozen in the same spot, the debugger still open. Remove the breakpoint, Proceed: it juggles on.
spoken: [excited] Relaunch, and everything's back, frozen right where we left it. Remove the breakpoint, proceed, and [pause] it juggles on.

caption: The VM is written in Smalltalk: the VM Simulator boots a guest image on those very classes. Change the VM's banner, ⌘S: the guest's next line shows it.
spoken: [excited] The VM itself is written in Smalltalk, so here's Smalltalk running inside Smalltalk! The guest's VM is the very classes in the browser. Change its banner, save, and [pause] the guest picks it up on its next line.

caption: Rebuild and reboot: translate the VM to C, compile, save the image, and the host restarts on the new VM.
spoken: Now rebuild: translate to C, compile, reboot, and [pause] the host itself runs the new VM!

caption: No hand-written C: in the Terminal (Smalltalk too), the VM's Smalltalk sources and the C generated from them.
spoken: Last thing! How much of this is hand-written C? Let's ask a terminal, which, yes, is Smalltalk too. [pause] None of it: the VM is Smalltalk, and every line of its C is generated from it.

caption: All of it live, in one running image, driven through samaltak-ctl.
spoken: [warm] All of that, live, in one running image. Thanks for watching!
